title: Underived canonical open base-change compatibility
statement: Let $U'\xrightarrow{g_U}U$ and $X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ form an open-immersion square with open immersions $j:U\to X$ and $j':U'\to X'$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Let $b_{g,F}:g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^{-1}F$ be the canonical map of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], and let $\beta_F:j'_!g_U^{-1}F\to g^{-1}j_!F$ be the module base-change map of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] for this square, read through the identifications $\kappa$ of the etale extensions by zero along $j$ and $j'$ with $j_!$ and $j'_!$ [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement]. Then $b_{g,F}=\beta_F^{-1}$. More explicitly, under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ the map $b_{g,F}^{-1}$ is the transpose of $s_g\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$, where $\eta_{j,F}:F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ is the extension-by-zero unit and $s_g:g_U^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ is the module-linear cartesian inverse-image identification. After identifying both restrictions with $g_U^{-1}F$ through these units and $s_g$, the restriction of $b_{g,F}$ is the identity.

source.place: Tags 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) and 0F70 (lemma-jshriek-open), with the module-mate construction in the project's base-change definition

proof.text:
Put $A=j_!F$, $N=g^{-1}A$, and write $\eta^g,\varepsilon^g$ for the unit and counit of $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, and $\eta^{g_U},\varepsilon^{g_U}$ for those of $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$. These are the module adjunctions of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The square comparison $s_g:g_U^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ is the inverse-image comparison of the flipped square in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. Its components are module-linear: it is a composite of the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] and their inverses. Denote the module underived exchange for that flipped square by $E:j^{-1}g_*\to g_{U*}j'^{-1}$. It is a natural transformation on modules by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear]. By its defining adjunction formula, its transpose at any module sheaf $P$ on $X'$ is
$$\varepsilon^{g_U}_{j'^{-1}P}\circ g_U^{-1}(E_P)=j'^{-1}(\varepsilon^g_P)\circ s_{g_*P}.$$
This is just the definition of exchange, with $f=g$, $f'=g_U$ and the two horizontal arrows $j,j'$.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), comparison of the right adjoints, expanded using the module exchange definition

proof.text:
The definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] is applied to the square of Step 1: its $f,f',j,j'$ are $g,g_U,j,j'$, its square isomorphism is $\theta=s_g$, and its formulas use only the commutative square and $\theta$; the cartesian identification is the chosen one of [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. That definition uses the etale extensions by zero along $j,j'$ with the adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. By [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement] for $j$ and for $j'$, the isomorphisms $\kappa$ identify these functors with the extensions by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and carry units to units and counits to counits of the adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]; transporting $\beta_F$ along $\kappa$ (as the statement does) therefore gives the same formula with $\eta_j,\eta_{j'},\varepsilon_{j'}$ the units and counits of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], which is the adjunction defining $b_{g,F}$. With this reading, the definition says that $\beta_F$ is the transpose, under $j'_!g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}j'^{-1}$, of
$$t=E_N\circ j^{-1}(\eta^g_A)\circ\eta_{j,F}:F\longrightarrow g_{U*}j'^{-1}N.$$
Here its displayed formula for $\eta_{1,F}$ is exactly $j^{-1}(\eta^g_A)\circ\eta_{j,F}$. The hom bijection for a composite adjunction is the composite of the two hom bijections [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Therefore, writing $\delta$ for the transpose of $\beta_F$ under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$, its transpose under $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$ is $t$. Applying the inverse hom bijection gives
$$\delta=\varepsilon^{g_U}_{j'^{-1}N}\circ g_U^{-1}(E_N)\circ g_U^{-1}j^{-1}(\eta^g_A)\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F}).$$

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), proof: the two composite adjunctions; explicit formula of the cited module-mate definition

proof.text:
Substitute Step 1 at $P=N$ in the formula for $\delta$. Naturality of the comparison $s_g$ along $\eta^g_A:A\to g_*N$ gives
$$s_{g_*N}\circ g_U^{-1}j^{-1}(\eta^g_A)=j'^{-1}g^{-1}(\eta^g_A)\circ s_A.$$
Consequently
$$\delta=j'^{-1}\!\left(\varepsilon^g_N\circ g^{-1}(\eta^g_A)\right)\circ s_A\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})=s_A\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F}).$$
The last equality is the triangle identity for $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, at $A$, since $N=g^{-1}A$; the module units and counits are those of the underlying abelian adjunction by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. This is solely functoriality, naturality, and the defining adjunction identities. All domains are module sheaves on $U'$ and all arrows were identified as linear in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); categories.tex Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), unit/counit description and triangle identity

proof.text: The characterization in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] says precisely that $b_{g,F}^{-1}$ has transpose $s_A\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$ under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Step 3 gives the same transpose for $\beta_F$ (read through $\kappa$ as in Step 2). The hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is given by the same sectionwise formula for every commutative $\Lambda$, so it commutes with forgetting the module structures; its injectivity for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ gives equality of the underlying abelian maps, $b_{g,F}^{-1}=\beta_F$, and in particular $b_{g,F}$ is $\Lambda$-linear. Since $b_{g,F}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], $\beta_F$ is invertible and $b_{g,F}=\beta_F^{-1}$; for the fibre-product square this invertibility is also [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. In particular Step 3 gives the requested explicit transpose for $b_{g,F}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tags 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) and 0F70 (lemma-jshriek-open), uniqueness via the extension-by-zero adjunction

proof.text:
Set $H=g_U^{-1}F$, $a=\eta_{j',H}:H\to j'^{-1}j'_!H$ and $d=s_A\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F}):H\to j'^{-1}N$. Both $a$ and $d$ are isomorphisms: [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] gives the unit isomorphisms on underlying abelian sheaves. They are isomorphisms on module sheaves too, because they are linear and their inverses are linear (if $v$ is a linear bijection, $v^{-1}(\lambda y)=\lambda v^{-1}(y)$ follows by applying $v$; inverses commute with sheaf restrictions by cancellation). By the definition of transpose for the module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], Step 3 says
$$j'^{-1}(\beta_F)\circ a=d.$$
Taking inverses and using $b_{g,F}=\beta_F^{-1}$ gives
$$a^{-1}\circ j'^{-1}(b_{g,F})\circ d=\mathrm{id}_H.$$
This is exactly the asserted restriction identity with both restrictions identified through the units and $s_g$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-fb1c9c7e3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 5 steps and every cited statement, plus the nodes that β's definition rests on: etale-sum-extension, etale-restriction-injectives (statement and proof), extension-by-zero, cartesian-square, underived-exchange (with blueprint_update). I also read unit sk-prop-sf-cbc, the parent cor and its main-20261015 blueprint text, and Stacks 03S3, 03S5, 0F70, 03S6 (etale-cohomology) and 03DI (sites-modules). I recomputed Steps 1, 3 and 5. Step 1: the exchange transpose formula, with s_g=θ in the right direction. Step 3: naturality plus the triangle identity gives δ=s_A∘g_U^{-1}η_{j,F}. Step 5: a^{-1}∘j'^{-1}(b)∘d=id. Edge cases checked: U empty, F=0, Λ=0, g=id, j=id. Fault 1 (C3/E6, silent identification): b uses the explicit open-immersion j_! and adjunction (lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction). β (def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map) uses the étale sum extension and the adjunction of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives, whose statement does not give a unit. In slopmaster2 these are separate constructions (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction vs etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction) and no lemma relates them. Step 2 and Steps 4–5 equated the two units and counits without a citation. The identification is true by Stacks 03DI. Repair: I added the statement-only node lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement. It says the sectionwise identification κ: j_!→j^et_! is a natural isomorphism that takes units to units and counits to counits. The item statement now reads β through κ (conclusion unchanged, nothing weakened), and Step 2 cites the new node. Fault 2 (Step 4): the delivery used the module hom bijection for b, which is a priori only an abelian map, and cited the fibre-product-only lemma lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules for β invertible. Step 4 now compares underlying abelian maps through the Λ-independent sectionwise bijection, and gets β invertible from b being an isomorphism. I recomputed proof_deps. The new node records only grep searches, because LeanSearch, Loogle and LeanFinder are not reachable here; it may need the other two search kinds added on the Codex machine. Mathlib's leftAdjointUniq is a generic iso of left adjoints; it does not give that iso as κ, so the verdict is no match. I accepted the three declared tool uses.
